An operator scheduling pause is recorded at first sight; a queue wait (a held instance, a retry backoff, an activity interval or any other deferral) or an unavailable instance only at an evaluation where the pair's activity window is closed, that is once the wait outlasted the window. gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:deferred:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>; it carries the same values as clock_slot_refused. A later refusal of the same occurrence because its window closed is not recorded.
clock_slot_deferred.common_causes: An operator paused scheduling across the slot; another claim held the instance until the activity window closed; the instance stayed unavailable until the window closed.
clock_slot_deferred.handling: Nothing to repair for an operator pause. For a wait that outlasted the window, check what held the instance (actingctl status) or why it stayed unavailable.

clock_slot_owed.description: A policy dispatch selected for a task on an instance (task_id, alias) serves a clock occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) from before the activity window it was selected in opened (window_start_unix_ms); for a daily-limited task it uses the new day's budget for an earlier slot. first_run is true when the pair had no earlier dispatch; next_occurrence_unix_ms is the next clock occurrence, so a reader can tell whether the run still served this occurrence. Recorded once, at the first cycle that selects the pair for that occurrence, as a goal_missed planning signal whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:owed:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>.
clock_slot_owed.common_causes: The slot fell while the activity window was closed or the Runtime was not running; a gate held the slot back the day before; a catalog was activated with new task ids outside the window.
clock_slot_owed.handling: Nothing to repair for a single owed run. Owed runs every morning together with refusals of the day's own slot mean that the slot's daily budget is displaced: gate the slot with its own timeline window or move it to the window start.

clock_slot_refused.description: A persistent gate refused a due clock slot of a policy task on an instance (task_id, alias): a budget (policy_budget_exhausted, with budget_dimension), a closed activity window, a task paused by failure suspension, or the configuration (the task disabled for the instance, a missing capability or activity profile). gate_code is the gate's own code. Recorded once per task, instance and occurrence (occurrence_unix_ms) as a goal_missed planning signal whose fact_code is this code followed by key=value tokens and whose signal_id is signal:clock_slot:refused:<sha256 of task, alias and occurrence>. window_end_unix_ms is the end of the activity window open at the refusal, next_eligible_unix_ms the first time the pair may be admitted again, next_occurrence_unix_ms the next clock occurrence.
clock_slot_refused.common_causes: A daily or window budget already used that day, often by an owed run that served the previous day's slot; the activity window closed before the slot could run; the task is paused after repeated failures; the task is disabled for the instance, or the instance lacks the operation or a matching activity profile.
clock_slot_refused.handling: Compare next_eligible_unix_ms with next_occurrence_unix_ms: below it, the slot runs later in the same or the next window; at or above it, the slot is lost to the next occurrence. Change the catalog (budget, slot times, activity window) or the instance configuration if the slot must run.

The state read after the failure is applied (a stopped instance is pending, with device.connected false) and carried on the record, which is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal. Until slice A2 turns it into a caused_by link, the control failure behind it is carried as the token cause=<code>, emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed.

After an expired wait the Start phase still runs (start_dispatched true); after any other Stop failure it does not. The restart fails whatever its Start did, and the record carries the last observed state; it is the request's one failure record and its receipt terminal, written after the Start phase when one ran. Until slice A2 turns it into a caused_by link, the control failure behind it is carried as the token cause=<code>, emulator_control_wait_timeout or emulator_control_failed.
emulator_restart_stop_failed.common_causes: The vendor's shutdown of the instance hung, for example its device process stayed after Android stopped (device_process_present true), or MuMuManager refused the shutdown.

lease_busy.description: An immediate try for an instance met a holder, or an eligible waiting entry that nobody may jump (Workflow #369). A Lab operation's refusal names who is in the way, before any frame or input: holder_kind is the holder's kind on a held instance, or the waiting entry's kind on a free one, where queue_position is that entry's position. A client AcquireLease and the Runtime's dedicated leases are refused with this code too. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_busy.common_causes: Another client, a scheduled run, a stuck-recovery ladder or an operator request holds the instance or waits for it.
lease_busy.handling: Nothing ran. Retry once the instance is free; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count.

Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_expired.common_causes: A holder that overran its own step bound; a host that was stopping while a ladder held an instance.

lease_queue_expired.description: An operator request waited its cap in its instance's one queue without a grant, and its entry was removed (Workflow #369). The waiting requests are a direct task run (CLI, console, MCP ac_run_pack; cap min(60 s, the run's remaining deadline minus a 30 s run budget)), a safe reset or an application lifecycle command (3 s), and a self-check or the reconnect of an instance resume (3 s; a resume is refused before its gate is lifted). timeout_ms is the cap; holder_kind names the instance's holder when it has one; queue_position is the entry's position when it was removed. Its ledger record is the instance-linked scheduler.denied lease_queue_expired at warning. A client QueueLease whose wait ended is refused with this code too. Registered once in the contract (A2a D3); the host and the scheduler emit it.
lease_queue_expired.common_causes: Another client, a scheduled run, a stuck-recovery ladder or another operator request held the instance for longer than the cap; a takeover cooldown after an unclean restart; business capacity refused the grant for the whole cap.
lease_queue_expired.handling: Nothing ran. Retry once the holder named by holder_kind has released the instance; actingctl status shows lease_active and queued_request_count meanwhile.

policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.description: After a start's reconciliation, a scheduled dispatch (its task's procedure is one the policy driver runs as a scheduled run) still has no outcome. The start settles every scheduled dispatch it can; this one stays open, and a later dispatch on its instance may be refused as a conflict. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.common_causes: The run's instance is no longer in the configuration, or the run's lease ended in more than one way (for example two transfers).
policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open.handling: Report it with the run id: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. When the instance was removed from the configuration, adding it back lets the next start settle the run.

policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.description: A start could not settle a scheduled run: the host's recovery or the ledger refused its settlement (failure_code is the refusal's code). The start carries on: the run's dispatch stays open, out of the active workloads, and the run's instance is paused with this code as the pause reason, so no new dispatch meets the open one. Recorded once per start, under the run's links, which carry the run id; lease_id is present when the dispatch has one lease grant.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.common_causes: A run whose recorded facts do not fit any settlement the Runtime knows, for example a ledger written by a defect in an earlier version.
policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled.handling: Report it with the run id and failure_code: the open dispatch needs a fix in the Runtime. After looking, lift the instance's scheduling pause (resume scheduling for the instance) to let other tasks dispatch there again; the open dispatch itself stays open until a version that can settle it starts.

policy_settlement_interrupted.description: A code several owners emit with one meaning (contract-owned, A2a D3): policy settlement interrupted.

policy_settlement_release_recovered.description: A start found a scheduled run whose dispatch has no outcome and whose lease has no lease.released under its run links, wrote the missing release (effect not_performed) and settles the run once: from its terminal when it has one, otherwise as interrupted (policy_settlement_interrupted), so the dispatch is closed; the first such interruption of its pair in a row is lifted by the same start. Recorded once, under the run's links, which carry the run id.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.common_causes: The Runtime ended between a run's task terminal and its lease end (for example inside a failed run's hand-off to its stuck-recovery ladder), in the middle of a run (a reboot or a killed process), or after a scheduled dispatch's lease grant and before its run's first task event.
policy_settlement_release_recovered.handling: Nothing to repair: the run counts as its terminal says, or as interrupted when it has none. A second interruption of the same pair in a row keeps the pair paused until its package changes, as for any interrupted settlement.

selection_evaluation_aborted.description: Retired. A scheduling-layer selection document met an unknown input under an abort_evaluation clause, and the whole scheduling evaluation failed for every instance. Since 0.12.0 the scheduling layer defers only the candidate that read the input (fact_refresh_unbound or selection_input_unknown) and the round goes on.
selection_evaluation_aborted.common_causes: An instance fact the document reads was missing or expired on one instance while the document declared abort_evaluation for it.
selection_evaluation_aborted.handling: None in 0.12.0 and later: the code is no longer emitted. Before 0.12.0, refresh the fact or change the clause to drop_candidate.

selection_input_unknown.description: A gate or term (rule_id) of a scheduling-layer selection document met an unknown input (unknown_reason) for a candidate on the instance that no reading can supply: an instruction key or pack data no instruction supplied, a fixed field, or a lookup that covers no value. Only that candidate is deferred, with no wake; it is evaluated again when the instance facts or the catalog change. One entry is written per rule that met such an input.
selection_input_unknown.common_causes: An instruction key (session.) was never set for the instance; the document's lookup lacks an entry and a default for a value the candidate has; the document reads a field the candidate does not carry.
selection_input_unknown.handling: Supply the instruction for the instance, or fix the selection document (add the lookup entry or default, or read a field the scheduling layer provides) and approve the catalog again.

selection_record_too_large.description: Event or record sanitization refused a value: selection record too large.

selection_unknown_clause_ignored.description: A gate or term (rule_id) of a scheduling-layer selection document declares a drop_candidate or substitute clause (unknown_clause) that the scheduling layer does not apply: there an unknown input defers the candidate that read it. The document's author meant something else than what runs. An abort_evaluation clause gives no warning.
selection_unknown_clause_ignored.common_causes: A selection document written for an in-task select step, where the clauses apply, is used as the scheduling-layer document.
selection_unknown_clause_ignored.handling: Expect the candidate to be deferred instead of dropped or scored with the substitute; to keep the clause's effect, use the document in a select step instead.
